page: Microsoft Azure E96ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs and 768.0 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains zero GPUs and features no local ephemeral storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage.

As part of the Env6 family, the configuration is network-optimized and engineered for throughput-intensive enterprise deployments. The lack of integrated local disk volumes means that all data persistence and operating system storage must be mounted via external storage solutions. This architecture isolates compute and memory resources from local storage failures, though it introduces dependency on external network storage latency and input/output capabilities.

Given the high memory capacity paired with 96 dedicated vCPUs, the E96ns_v6 provides high resource density for workloads demanding extensive in-memory footprints without requiring hardware acceleration. Typical applications include large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, high-capacity caching layers, heavy extract-transform-load (ETL) processing pipelines, and large-scale data analytics jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ns_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel processor and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 96 dedicated vCPUs and 768.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Belonging to the network-optimized Env6 series, it supports Premium Storage integrations. The instance does not bundle local ephemeral storage drives, requiring workloads to utilize external storage volumes for operating system disks and persistent file data. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated. The combination of dense dedicated CPU capacity and expansive memory makes this server suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks that do not depend on local disk arrays. Suitable deployment profiles include enterprise relational database management systems, large in-memory key-value caches, analytical data processing pipelines, and large-scale business applications.
